headline: High-risk shared filesystem and write-capable pair create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and run browsers; Plandex reads/writes the project directory and supports stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where one agent’s files or outputs can be consumed by the other as instructions. The pair is not isolated by default, so injection risk exists without unusual setup.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or exchanged files
IF either agent treats file contents as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Require human review before copying outputs between agents
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write local files, and ECC explicitly touches session summaries, hooks, MCP configs, and security findings while Plandex operates on a project directory plus plan-local sandbox. Shared workspace use can expose sensitive code or operational data from one agent to the other, even though neither profile proves uncontrolled exfiltration by default.
conditions: IF the same directory contains secrets, logs, or security findings
IF outputs from one agent are copied into the other without filtering
mitigations: Keep secrets outside both workspaces
Use separate OS users or containers
Redact logs before sharing artifacts
Restrict file permissions on shared directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC and Plandex both have shell execution, filesystem write, and git-state modification. ECC also supports multiple instances with shared-state warnings, while Plandex shares state via a backend. Concurrent writes to the same repo or plan can corrupt work or overwrite changes, and the default overlap is dangerous without explicit coordination.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository
IF either agent auto-applies changes while the other is editing
mitigations: Assign one writer at a time
Use separate branches per agent
Require manual merge review
Pause one agent before the other writes
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate findings, documentation, and agent outputs; Plandex is a review-then-apply coding tool that can act on plan outputs. If Plandex treats ECC’s output as authoritative, mistakes or hallucinations can cascade into committed code or staged changes. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Plandex consumes ECC-produced text as the source of truth
IF auto-apply is enabled or review is skipped
mitigations: Require independent verification of ECC outputs
Disable auto-apply
Have Plandex cite original sources before acting
Use a human approval gate for commits
requires-engineering: add structured handoff validation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. ECC does handle session and security-related data classes, but Plandex only lists source code and model-provider keys. With no explicit cross-border or regulated-data pathway documented, compliance risk is limited and mainly depends on what data the operator places into the shared workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared project directory
IF retention settings differ for the same data class across the two tools
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Align retention settings before use
Review logging defaults
Use separate storage for sensitive artifacts
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
